deliverables: WP1 - Plutarch and Ply Maintenance, Compatibility & Developer Experience
Bug fixes, correctness improvements, and optimizations
Documentation, examples, technical blog posts, and developer-experience improvements
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor MLabs
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund annual maintenance and enhancement of MLabs Core Tool Maintenance & Enhancement: Plutarch and Ply.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada, consisting of 1,128,880 ada for Plutarch and Ply maintenance, compatibility, and developer experience plus a 33,866 ada Intersect administration fee.

Plutarch is described as a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts via controlled compilation into UPLC, while Ply serializes Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types.
The proposal says MLabs counted at least 26 teams using Plutarch and Ply in the motivation section, while the rationale separately says the count was at least 15 teams.

The proposal states that Plutarch scripts rank among the smallest in MLabs' public cross-language benchmark suite while requiring comparatively low on-chain compute and memory, and links to the benchmark page.
The next funding period is expected to cover ongoing Cardano ledger, Plutus, and tooling evolution, including possible Dijkstra-era compatibility if relevant changes land during the funding period.
The proposal claims that if Plutarch and Ply fall behind ledger and Plutus/UPLC evolution, existing adopters may face more friction, migration risk, bespoke workarounds, or avoidable rewrites.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation, final audited results, and an audit report.
The proposal asserts that the requested amount does not breach the 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission and links to the relevant governance action.

The proposal states that Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with a TRSC, one PSSC, named contract addresses, multisignature permission thresholds, and an external Oversight Committee of six entities.
The document discloses prior MLabs funding from listed treasury actions, Project Catalyst Fund9 and Fund13 awards, and a 70,000 ada Intersect payment for Conway-era Plutarch updates.

summary: The document requests 1,162,746 ada for MLabs Plutarch and Ply maintenance through Intersect-administered smart contracts, describes technical and ecosystem benefits, provides external references for voting, benchmarks, prior funding, NCL compliance, and treasury-contract oversight, but some adoption and risk-reduction claims are proposer assertions and the team-count figures differ within the text.
